# package mqtt

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/notification/mqtt"
```

Package mqtt is the MQTT binding of OpenADR 3 notifications, for both sides: Publisher sends a VTN's notifications to a broker, and Subscriber receives them in a client.

The broker is not part of this module: a VTN that notifies by MQTT runs one, and its access control decides who may read which topic. See SECURITY.md.

## Types

### type Broker

```go
type Broker struct {
	// URL is the address of the broker: mqtt://host:1883 or mqtts://host:8883.
	URL string
	// ClientID identifies this client to the broker. Two connections with
	// the same ID take each other's place, so it has to be unique among the
	// clients of the broker. When empty the broker assigns one.
	ClientID string
	Username string
	Password string
	// TLS configures a connection to an mqtts URL; the defaults of
	// crypto/tls when nil.
	TLS *tls.Config
	// Backoff is the wait before a second attempt to connect, doubled for
	// each one after, up to a minute; 1 second when zero. It is also the
	// wait, doubled in the same way, before connecting again after a
	// connection that was lost: a broker that drops every connection at
	// once is not dialled again at once.
	Backoff time.Duration
}
```

Broker says how to reach and log in to a broker.

### type LateAckMetrics

```go
type LateAckMetrics interface {
	// OnLateAck is called for an acknowledgement (PUBACK, SUBACK or
	// UNSUBACK) of a packet identifier that no request of the connection
	// waits for: the answer to a publish or a subscription that was given
	// up on, which came after all, or one that answers nothing. It is
	// dropped, and completes no other request. OnLateAck runs on the
	// goroutine that reads the connection. Like the other callbacks it must
	// not block, and one that does not return normally is logged in the
	// same way.
	OnLateAck()
}
```

LateAckMetrics is an extension of Metrics: a Metrics value of a Publisher or a Subscriber that also has OnLateAck is told of every acknowledgement from the broker that nothing waits for.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnConnected is called when a connection to the broker is made, and,
	// for a Subscriber, the subscriptions with it.
	OnConnected()
	// OnDisconnected is called when a connection is lost or given up, with
	// the reason.
	OnDisconnected(err error)
	// OnPublished is called when the broker has confirmed a notification.
	OnPublished()
	// OnDropped is called when a notification is not queued, because the
	// queue is full: the broker has been away for too long. It is also
	// called for a notification that MQTT cannot carry, a topic with a
	// wildcard or NUL or a topic or body too long, which is dropped
	// instead of sent again.
	OnDropped()
	// OnReceived is called for every notification a Subscriber hands to
	// its Notify function, before it does. A notification is not handed
	// to Notify when the Subscriber was closed meanwhile, by OnReceived
	// for one.
	OnReceived()
}
```

Metrics receives a callback for what a Publisher or a Subscriber does. A Publisher calls OnPublished and OnDropped, a Subscriber OnReceived, and both the two about the connection. The callbacks run on the goroutines of the Publisher or Subscriber, or for OnDropped on the caller's of Publish, and must not block. They run without a lock of the Publisher or Subscriber held, but OnReceived, which runs as Notify does: one at a time, and a Close on another goroutine waits for it. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

A callback that does not return normally is logged at error level, as "mqtt: callback did not return normally" with the fields callback, value and stack, and the Publisher or Subscriber goes on as if it had returned. So is the handler of the Logger, which loses that entry.

### type Publisher

```go
type Publisher struct {

	// running bounds what run waits for; Close ends it, with stop. It is a
	// pointer so that Publisher stays comparable.

	// waitedFor are the goroutines Close waits for: that of run, and one
	// that reads a connection while it is in OnLateAck, which run may wait
	// for. A Close on one of them does not wait. A pointer, as running.

}
```

Publisher sends notifications to a broker, in the order they were given, at QoS 1. While the broker cannot be reached they wait, up to the size of the queue, and the connection is tried again.

Delivery to the broker is at least once while the Publisher runs. It is not durable: what is queued when the process stops is lost. What the broker does for a client that is not connected is the broker's business; with the clean sessions the Subscriber of this package uses, such a client misses the message.

A Publisher is safe for concurrent use. Close it to stop it.

#### func NewPublisher

```go
func NewPublisher(cfg PublisherConfig) (*Publisher, error)
```

NewPublisher returns a running Publisher. It does not wait for the broker: the connection is made in the background.

#### func (Publisher) Close

```go
func (p *Publisher) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close stops accepting notifications and waits until those that are queued have reached the broker, or until ctx ends, whichever is first. It may be called more than once and from several goroutines at the same time; each call waits in the same way.

Close may also be called from the Metrics callbacks and the Logger's handler. On a goroutine of the Publisher, which it would wait for, it does not wait: it stops accepting notifications and returns nil at once, and the Publisher goes on, once that callback has returned, until what is queued has reached the broker or ctx has ended, as it does for a Close on another goroutine. OnDropped for a full queue, and its log entry, run on the goroutine that called Publish: a Close there waits.

#### func (Publisher) Publish

```go
func (p *Publisher) Publish(topic string, body []byte)
```

Publish queues a notification for a topic and returns at once.

### type Subscriber

```go
type Subscriber struct {

	// closed while subscribed

	// calling is held while Notify runs, so that Close can wait for it.

	// runner is the goroutine of run, and notifying the one in Notify
	// (0 when none): a Close called on one of them does not wait for it.

}
```

Subscriber receives the notifications a VTN publishes on a broker. It keeps the connection up: when it is lost, it connects and subscribes again.

What is published while the Subscriber is not connected is missed: it uses clean sessions. A message may arrive twice. As with webhooks, a client that must not miss a change still polls from time to time, and does so after every reconnect; Connected tells when.

#### func NewSubscriber

```go
func NewSubscriber(cfg SubscriberConfig) (*Subscriber, error)
```

NewSubscriber returns a running Subscriber. It does not wait for the broker; use Ready for that.

#### func (Subscriber) Close

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Close() error
```

Close disconnects and stops the Subscriber, and returns when it has stopped and a Notify in progress has returned. Notify is not called after Close has returned.

Close may be called more than once, from several goroutines at the same time, and from Notify, the Metrics callbacks and the Logger's handler. From one of those it does not wait for the callback it is called from, which goes on until it returns. Called from Notify, OnReceived or OnLateAck, it returns when the rest of the Subscriber has stopped. Called from OnConnected, OnDisconnected or the Logger's handler, it may return before that: the Subscriber stops once that callback has returned, and a Notify in progress goes on until it returns. In every case no Notify begins after Close has returned. A goroutine that Notify waits for is not Notify: a Close there waits for Notify, which must not wait for it.

#### func (Subscriber) Ready

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Ready(ctx context.Context) error
```

Ready waits until the Subscriber is connected and subscribed: from then on, what the VTN publishes is received.

#### func (Subscriber) Sessions

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Sessions() int
```

Sessions is the number of times the Subscriber has connected and subscribed. It grows by one with every reconnect: a client that polls after a reconnect watches it.

### type SubscriberConfig

```go
type SubscriberConfig struct {
	Broker
	// Topics are the topic filters to subscribe to, as a VTN names them in
	// its topic operations (see the MQTTTopics method of the clients).
	// Required.
	Topics []string
	// Notify is called for each notification, one at a time, in the order
	// the broker delivers them. Required. It should return soon: nothing
	// else is received meanwhile. It may call Close (see Close). A Notify
	// that does not return normally is logged at error level, as
	// "mqtt: callback did not return normally" with the fields callback,
	// value and stack; the message is acknowledged and the Subscriber
	// goes on with the next.
	Notify func(ctx context.Context, topic string, n openadr.Notification)
	// Logger receives connection failures and messages that are not
	// notifications. Nil disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Metrics receives a callback for what happens; see Metrics. Nil
	// disables them.
	Metrics Metrics
}
```

SubscriberConfig configures a Subscriber.
